problem.paragraph: 1. Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 1 to 6 in increments of 1 unit. The curve begins at the point (0, 5) on the y axis, goes down and to the right, bends down, reaches its low point at (1, 2), goes up and to the right through (2, 3), bends up like an arch, and reaches its high point at (3, 4). The curve then goes down and to the right, reaches its sharp low point at (4, 1), then goes up and to the right, now again bends up, and exits the viewing window at (6, 6). $$\left( {1,3} \right)$$ , $$\left( {4,6} \right)$$ $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {3,4} \right)$$ $$\left( {0,2} \right)$$ $$\left( {2,4} \right)$$ , $$\left( {4,6} \right)$$ $$\left( {2,3} \right)$$

2. Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 1 to 6 in increments of 1 unit. The curve begins at the origin, goes up and to the right, bends up like an arch, reaches its high point at (1, 3), goes down and to the right through (2, 2), now bending down, and reaches its low point at (3, 1). image.alt: Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from 0 to beyond 6 in increments of 1 unit. It then goes up and to the right through (3, 0), bends like an arch, reaches its high point at x = 4, then goes down and to the right, crosses the x axis at (5, 0), and exits the viewing window with its low point at x = 6 with a solid dot.

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from 0 to 8 in increments of 2 units. The curve enters the fourth quadrant near the y axis, goes up and to the right, crosses the x axis at (1, 0), concave down, reaches its high point at x = 2, then goes down and to the right, now becoming concave up, and reaches its low point at (4, 0) on the x axis. It then goes up and to the right, mirrors its earlier path by reaching its high point at x = 6, then goes down and to the right by crossing the x axis at (7, 0), and exits the fourth quadrant.

problem.paragraph: In an episode of The Simpsons television show, Homer reads from a newspaper and announces “Here’s good news! According to this eye-catching article, SAT scores are declining at a slower rate.” Interpret Homer’s statement in terms of a function and its first and second derivatives.
The president announces that the national deficit is increasing, but at a decreasing rate. Interpret this statement in terms of a function and its first and second derivatives.

solution.paragraph: If $$D(t)$$ is the size of the deficit as a function of time, then at the time of the speech $$D^{\prime}(t) > 0$$ , but $$D^{''}(t) < 0$$ .

problem.paragraph: A drug response curve describes the level of medication in the bloodstream after a drug is administered. A surge function $$S(t) = At^{p}e^{- kt}$$ is often used to model the response curve, reflecting an initial surge in the drug level and then a more gradual decline. If, for a particular drug, $$A = 0.01$$ , $$p = 4$$ , $$k = 0.07$$ and $$t$$ is measured in minutes, estimate the times corresponding to the inflection points and explain their significance. Then graph the drug response curve.

solution.paragraph: $$28.57$$ min, when the rate of increase of drug level in the bloodstream is greatest; $$85.71$$ min, when rate of decrease is greatest
